conclusion: Criterion authorship is not in the release, so a participant's RATINGS are the only available proxy for their values. Scoring each person's four responses with their own signed ratings and re-scoring with a stranger's ratings of EXACTLY the same criteria -- same set, different numbers, so nothing but the weights differs -- over 14,925 person-prompt cells: on the `world` block own weights reach 0.6430 against strangers' 0.6078, an advantage of +0.0398 [+0.0359, +0.0439]. HALF the assessments carrying a `personal` ranking give the SAME STRING as their `world` one (51.6%), and on those the two advantages are equal by construction, so the contrast is read only on the 1,547 cells where the two rankings actually differ: there the world advantage is +0.0356 [+0.0247, +0.0462] and the personal advantage +0.0332 [+0.0226, +0.0436]. On the `personal` block, which this campaign had never opened, the advantage is +0.0332 [+0.0226, +0.0436]. An oracle picking each cell's single best-aligned criterion reaches 0.9192, so the instrument can separate weightings; the same weights attached to the WRONG criteria score 0.5595. WORLD: W-SHARED-ONLY. Own ratings beat strangers', but by the same margin on the impersonal `world` block as on the explicitly personal one. Something was captured; it is not personal, and no person-level claim may rest on the ratings as a proxy for individual values.
